answers.assumption_check: Load-bearing: a commit subject naming a ticket id means the commit built or sealed that ticket (the integrator's convention; the census read subjects only). A subject can name another ticket in passing (e.g. 'a3ac, de75: ...'), so a false red is possible; the red lists the commits so a human can dismiss it. Not measured: how many of the 47 are such passing mentions.
answers.builder_check: A builder needs: the slot beside slate_reach in inspect(), _workflow_cursor, the single git log with --name-only, the code-path rule, the finding shape slate_reach emits, and a scratch repo plus commons fixture. The ticket names them.

answers.collision_check: Looked at 217c82fe7b57 (hollow anchoring: adjacent, different), history_integrity (working copy vs committed history, not cursor vs repo log), slate_reach and unbuilt_intentions (same wiring slot, different claim). No sieve compares the cursor with the repo log. RULE 1 holds: it reads records and imports no machine.
answers.falsifier_check: Clauses: (1) a code commit naming a TICKETME ticket is reported with its sha | (2) a doc-only commit, a ticket past TICKETME, and an unnamed TICKETME ticket are not reported. Horizon: red on current inspector.py (no such scan), green after; then the live scan lists the 47 minus the false positives.
